ad-fraud.meaning: This device looked up several ad domains in one window.
check: Compare the names with the loaded ad indicators.
See which app or page on the device loads those names.
benignCauses: A display loads an ad-funded page.
A vendor SDK fetches an ad network.

check: See whether the device is in a maintenance window.
Check who can reach the debug port.
benignCauses: A technician enabled debugging for a repair.
A lab image ships with debugging on.

alert-storm.meaning: This device produced more anomalies than its per-minute cap.
check: Read the detectors named in the recent anomalies.
See whether one event fan-out caused the burst.
benignCauses: A firmware update touches many new destinations at once.
A clock correction replays a burst of events.

answer-drift.meaning: A name resolved to an address it had not used before.
check: Compare the new answer with the resolver and the previous address.
See whether the name is a CDN or the device vendor.
benignCauses: A CDN rotates addresses.
A resolver returns a different site in a anycast set.

arp-spoof.meaning: Two different MAC addresses claimed the same IP.
check: Check the DHCP lease for that IP.
See whether a phone or laptop just joined the LAN.
benignCauses: A device renewed a lease and changed NIC.
A virtual machine moved to another host.

beacon-change.meaning: A regular destination changed its timing or peer.
check: Compare the new interval with the learned beacon.
See whether a firmware update shipped today.
benignCauses: A vendor changed the check-in interval.
The device rebooted and picked a new timer.

blockchain-c2.meaning: Traffic matched a known cryptocurrency or chain endpoint.
check: Confirm the destination against the indicator source.
See whether the device is a miner or a compromised camera.
benignCauses: A wallet app on a general-purpose device.
A lab host running a chain client.

bogon-destination.meaning: Outbound traffic went to an address that is not globally routable.
check: Check the destination against the bogon list.
See whether the device meant a LAN address.
benignCauses: A misconfigured DNS answer returned a private address.
A test harness uses a documentation address.

browser-mimic.meaning: A device class that is not a browser used a browser TLS fingerprint.
check: Confirm the device class is still correct.
See which process opened the TLS session.
benignCauses: A camera firmware added a browser-like stack.
The class tag is wrong for a tablet.

brute-force-in.meaning: Many short inbound attempts hit a login port.
check: See which source address sent the attempts.
Check whether that port is meant to be open.
benignCauses: A management scan from the operator.
A NAT hairpin retrying a closed service.

brute-force-out.meaning: This device made many short outbound attempts to a login port.
check: See the destination addresses and port.
Check whether the device should administer other hosts.
benignCauses: A controller polling several managed devices.
A mis-set port on a health check.

cert-change.meaning: The certificate issuer for a known name changed.
check: Compare the old and new issuer on that name.
See whether the vendor rotated certificates today.
benignCauses: A planned certificate rotation.
A CDN presented a different intermediate.

class-violation.meaning: The device did something its class prior does not allow.
check: Confirm the class set with setDeviceClass.
See which destination or port broke the prior.
benignCauses: The class tag is too narrow.
A new feature of the product uses an extra destination.

cleartext-regression.meaning: A host that had been using TLS was contacted in cleartext.
check: See the host and the port of the cleartext session.
Check whether a firmware update dropped TLS.
benignCauses: A local status page on port 80.
A captive portal before the encrypted session.

check: Check the sensor clock and NTP.
See whether events were replayed from a file.
benignCauses: The gateway clock stepped during boot.
A test replay used an earlier timestamp.

coap-amplification.meaning: This device answered a CoAP query in a way that can amplify.
check: See the source of the query and the response size.
Check whether CoAP is meant to face the WAN.
benignCauses: A local controller polling sensors.
A discovery burst on the LAN.

connection-churn.meaning: This device opened far more connections than its learned window.
check: Compare the count with the learned maximum.
See whether a retry loop is running.
benignCauses: A cloud reconnect after a WAN blip.
An app refresh that opens many short calls.

credential-stuffing-out.meaning: This device contacted many distinct login sites in one window.
check: List the site names in the anomaly.
See whether a person is using the device as a browser.
benignCauses: A smart display loading several account pages.
A test that walks a list of hostnames.

cryptomining.meaning: Traffic matched a mining protocol or pool.
check: Confirm the peer and the operation name.
See whether the device CPU is unexpectedly busy.
benignCauses: A lab host running a miner on purpose.
A general-purpose PC tagged as an appliance.

dga.meaning: Several generated-looking DNS names appeared in one window.
check: Read the sample name in the anomaly.
See whether the device should only use vendor names.
benignCauses: A CDN uses high-entropy labels.
A captive portal uses random hostnames.

dhcp-starvation.meaning: Many different MAC addresses sent DHCP discovers.
check: See whether a new switch or Wi-Fi client burst joined.
Check the DHCP server log for the same minute.
benignCauses: A classroom of devices booting together.
A phone randomizing its MAC on each probe.

direct-ip.meaning: Outbound traffic went to a public IP this device has not resolved.
check: See whether a later DNS answer explains the address.
Check the address against a threat feed if you have one.
benignCauses: A device with a hard-coded vendor address.
DNS happened on a resolver this sensor did not see.

dns-rebinding.meaning: A public name answered with a bogon address.
check: Compare the name and the answer address.
See whether the resolver is the one the device should use.
benignCauses: Split-horizon DNS for a local name.
A test resolver returning a lab address.

dns-tunnel.meaning: DNS queries carried more payload than a normal lookup.
check: Read the query name length and type.
See whether the device should only use short vendor names.
benignCauses: A security tool using DNS for telemetry.
A long TXT record from a vendor.

egress-flood.meaning: Outbound volume exceeded the flood limit.
check: Compare bytes and packets with the device baseline.
See whether a backup or camera upload is scheduled.
benignCauses: A camera uploading a clip.
A firmware download counted on the wrong direction.

failed-connection-ratio.meaning: Most connection attempts in the window failed.
check: See the destinations and the TCP outcome.
Check whether the remote service is down.
benignCauses: A service outage causing retries.
A scan of closed ports by a management tool.

fan-out.meaning: One window contacted more hosts than the learned limit.
check: List the hosts if the sensor still has them.
See whether a directory or cloud API fans out.
benignCauses: A hub talking to every paired device.
A DNS resolver contacting many authorities.

fast-flux.meaning: One name returned many short-lived addresses.
check: Compare the answer set and TTLs with earlier lookups.
See whether the name is a CDN.
benignCauses: A CDN with a low TTL.
A load balancer rotating backends.

fleet-wave.meaning: Several devices contacted the same new destination together.
check: See which devices share the destination.
Check whether a vendor push went out.
benignCauses: A firmware update rolling across a product line.
Devices booting and calling the same setup host.

gratuitous-arp-flood.meaning: Gratuitous ARP announcements exceeded the count limit.
check: See the IP and MAC in the announcements.
Check for a failover or a loop.
benignCauses: A clustered gateway failing over.
A device announcing itself after link up.

horizontal-scan.meaning: One port was touched on many hosts.
check: See the port and the host count.
Check whether a management scan is scheduled.
benignCauses: An inventory scan.
A controller probing paired devices.

icmp-redirect.meaning: An ICMP redirect tried to change a route.
check: See the source of the redirect.
Check the gateway address the device should use.
benignCauses: A router sending a legitimate redirect.
A lab topology with asymmetric routes.

icmp-tunnel.meaning: ICMP packets were large enough to carry a tunnel.
check: Compare bytes per packet with a normal ping.
See the peer address.
benignCauses: A path-MTU probe with a large packet.
A monitoring tool using ICMP echo.

identity-change.meaning: A MAC address presented a new DHCP fingerprint.
check: Compare the old and new fingerprints for that MAC.
See whether the NIC or the OS changed.
benignCauses: A firmware update changed the DHCP client.
A dock or USB ethernet adapter was inserted.

check: See the source address and destination port.
Check whether a port forward is intentional.
benignCauses: A vendor cloud connecting to a camera.
A person reaching a published service.

input-gap.meaning: The sensor stopped delivering events for this device.
check: Check the sensor and the span named in the anomaly.
See whether the device was powered off.
benignCauses: A planned maintenance window.
The device sleeping with no traffic.

ipv6-tunnel.meaning: Traffic used an IPv6 transition tunnel this device had not used.
check: See whether the kind is 6in4 or Teredo.
Check if the OS enabled IPv6 transition.
benignCauses: An OS update enabling Teredo.
A VPN client using 6in4.

lan-lateral.meaning: This device contacted a LAN peer it had not learned.
check: See the peer address.
Check whether a new device was paired.
benignCauses: A new phone on the LAN.
A hub talking to a newly installed sensor.

lan-sweep.meaning: ICMP or similar probes covered many LAN addresses.
check: See the address range.
Check whether an inventory tool is running.
benignCauses: A controller discovering devices.
A person running a LAN scan.

lan-via-proxy.meaning: After a proxy-like session, the device reached a LAN host.
check: Read the proxy peer and the later LAN peer.
See whether a remote support tool is installed.
benignCauses: A support session that then touches a local device.
A hub relaying a cloud command to a sensor.

long-connection.meaning: A single connection stayed open past the long-session limit.
check: See the peer and the duration.
Check whether a stream or tunnel is expected.
benignCauses: A camera stream.
A persistent cloud socket.

mqtt-new-broker.meaning: This device contacted an MQTT broker it had not used.
check: See the broker address and port.
Check whether the broker is the house broker.
benignCauses: A new hub broker after a migration.
A device shipped with a vendor broker.

mqtt-publish-rate.meaning: MQTT publishes exceeded the rate limit.
check: See the topic and the count.
Check whether a sensor is stuck in a loop.
benignCauses: A burst of retained status messages.
A controller pushing a configuration.

mqtt-topic-new.meaning: A publish used a topic this device had not used.
check: Read the topic.
See whether a new automation was added.
benignCauses: A new scene or device in the broker.
A firmware update adding a status topic.

mqtt-wildcard-subscribe.meaning: A client subscribed with a wildcard topic.
check: See which client and which pattern.
Check whether that client should see every topic.
benignCauses: An admin console subscribing to #.
A bridge mirroring the broker.

new-asn.meaning: Traffic went to an autonomous system this device had not used.
check: See the ASN and the destination.
Check whether a CDN or cloud region is new.
benignCauses: A vendor moved to another cloud ASN.
Anycast shifted to a different network.

check: See the destination and the interval.
Check whether a vendor check-in was added.
benignCauses: A new telemetry host after an update.
A device that only beacons after provisioning.

new-client-fingerprint.meaning: A TLS client fingerprint this device had not used appeared.
check: Compare the JA4 with the learned set.
See whether the firmware or OS changed.
benignCauses: A firmware update changed the TLS stack.
A library update on the device.

new-country.meaning: Traffic went to a country this device had not used.
check: See the country and the destination address.
Check whether a CDN edge is in a new region.
benignCauses: A CDN edge in another country.
A vendor support site hosted abroad.

new-destination.meaning: A destination name or address was not in the learned set.
check: See the destination.
Check whether it belongs to the vendor or a CDN.
benignCauses: A CDN hostname rotation.
A one-time firmware host.

new-device.meaning: A device identifier was seen for the first time.
check: Confirm the identifier is a device you installed.
See the first event time.
benignCauses: A new phone or sensor on the LAN.
A MAC change after a factory reset.

new-domain-family.meaning: A registrable domain family was not in the learned set.
check: See the family name.
Check whether a sibling of a known vendor domain is expected.
benignCauses: A vendor adding a new product domain.
A CDN family the device had not needed yet.

new-port.meaning: A destination port was not in the learned set.
check: See the port and the peer.
Check whether a new service was enabled.
benignCauses: A vendor moving from one TLS port to another.
A local admin page on a high port.

new-protocol.meaning: A protocol this device had not used appeared.
check: See the protocol.
Check whether a feature such as a tunnel was turned on.
benignCauses: An OS update enabling a new transport.
A paired accessory using a new protocol.

ntp-rogue.meaning: Time queries went to an NTP server this device had not used.
check: See the server address.
Check the gateway NTP setting.
benignCauses: A new router advertising itself as NTP.
A device falling back to a public NTP pool.

nxdomain-burst.meaning: Failed DNS lookups exceeded the learned count.
check: Read the sample names.
See whether a suffix or search list is wrong.
benignCauses: A device retrying a retired vendor name.
A search domain appending a local suffix.

check: See the operation and the caller.
Check whether a technician is in the camera UI.
benignCauses: A person editing the camera.
A VMS applying a profile.

ot-dangerous-op.meaning: An operational-technology call used a dangerous operation.
check: See the operation, target, and peer.
Check whether a maintenance window is open.
benignCauses: A technician writing a setpoint.
A programmed control sequence.

ot-error-burst.meaning: Operational-technology errors exceeded the burst limit.
check: See the operation and the error count.
Check the controller log for the same minute.
benignCauses: A sensor offline causing repeated reads.
A scan of points that are not installed.

ot-new-master.meaning: A new peer acted as an OT master.
check: See the peer address.
Check whether a new engineering station was connected.
benignCauses: A backup controller coming online.
A technician laptop on the OT network.

ot-recon.meaning: OT discovery or enumeration exceeded the recon limit.
check: See the operations and the peer.
Check whether an asset inventory is running.
benignCauses: A controller browsing points at startup.
An engineering tool listing devices.

ot-spoof.meaning: An OT identity was claimed from a new peer address.
check: Compare the peer with the learned owner of that target.
See whether a controller failed over.
benignCauses: A redundant controller taking the identity.
A device that changed address after a reboot.

ot-value-out-of-range.meaning: A written value fell outside the learned range.
check: See the target, the value, and the learned min and max.
Check whether the process setpoint was changed on purpose.
benignCauses: A seasonal setpoint change.
A commissioning step writing a new range.

ot-wan-exposure.meaning: An OT port was reachable from outside the plant LAN.
check: See the port and the source.
Check firewall rules for that port.
benignCauses: A remote support path left open.
A VPN address classified as outside.

ot-write-new.meaning: A write targeted a point this device had not written.
check: See the target name.
Check whether a new control point was added.
benignCauses: A new schedule or scene.
Commissioning of a new point.

check: See the target and the count.
Check for a control loop that is oscillating.
benignCauses: A startup sequence writing many points.
A person jogging a setpoint.

p2p-pattern.meaning: The flow pattern matched peer-to-peer relay behavior.
check: See the peers and ports.
Check whether the camera uses a vendor P2P cloud.
benignCauses: A camera vendor P2P relay.
A game or voice app on a general-purpose device.

packet-flood.meaning: Packet rate exceeded the flood limit.
check: Compare packets with the device baseline.
See the peer and protocol.
benignCauses: A camera stream.
A burst of discovery packets.

peer-divergence.meaning: This device contacted a destination its peer group does not use.
check: See the destination and the group.
Check whether this unit is a different product revision.
benignCauses: One unit on a newer firmware.
A device placed in the wrong peer group.

policy-violation.meaning: Traffic matched a policy the operator loaded.
check: Read the policy id in the anomaly.
See whether that policy is still intended.
benignCauses: A policy that is broader than the network.
A test that hits the blocked port.

post-update-drift.meaning: Behavior shifted after an update marker.
check: See what changed after the update event.
Check the firmware version if the sensor has it.
benignCauses: A firmware update that adds a destination.
A configuration push after an update.

posture-cleartext-auth.meaning: A login protocol ran in cleartext.
check: See the port. Telnet is 23 and FTP is 21.
Check whether the device can use SSH or TLS instead.
benignCauses: A legacy printer that only speaks FTP.
A lab device left on telnet.

posture-listening-risky.meaning: A risky port accepted a connection.
check: See the port and the direction.
Check whether that service should be bound.
benignCauses: A camera admin port used by the VMS.
A building controller listening on a vendor port.

posture-wan-exposed.meaning: A public address reached an open port on this device.
check: See the port and the source address.
Check the port-forward and firewall rules.
benignCauses: A published camera or web UI.
A cloud provider health check.

posture-weak-tls.meaning: A TLS session used an old version or a weak certificate.
check: See the reason in the anomaly.
Check whether the peer can be upgraded.
benignCauses: An old printer that only offers TLS 1.0.
A self-signed device certificate.

private-answer-for-public-name.meaning: A public name resolved to a private address.
check: Compare the name and the answer.
See whether split-horizon DNS is intentional.
benignCauses: Split-horizon DNS for an internal site.
A resolver rewriting a name to a local cache.

protocol-mix-shift.meaning: The mix of protocols departed from the learned mix.
check: See which protocol grew.
Check for a new feature or a tunnel.
benignCauses: A firmware update adding UDP.
A backup path using a different transport.

proxy-backconnect.meaning: A long control session was followed by many short outbound bursts.
check: See the control peer and the later destinations.
Check for a remote-access tool.
benignCauses: A support agent connected, then the device checked in.
A cloud command channel with fan-out.

proxy-relay.meaning: Traffic matched a known proxy or relay.
check: Confirm the indicator or the port.
See whether the device should use a corporate proxy.
benignCauses: An intentional HTTP proxy.
A vendor relay for a camera.

proxy-sdk-traffic.meaning: A name matched the proxy-SDK indicator list.
check: Confirm the name against the list source.
See which application on the device uses it.
benignCauses: A smart-TV SDK the vendor ships.
A test indicator loaded for a lab.

quic-new.meaning: QUIC appeared to a peer this device had not used.
check: See the peer address.
Check whether a browser or app update enabled QUIC.
benignCauses: A CDN turning on HTTP/3.
An app update using QUIC.

reflection-participation.meaning: This device answered a query that can be used for reflection.
check: See the protocol and the source of the query.
Check whether that service should face untrusted hosts.
benignCauses: A local resolver answering LAN clients.
An NTP server for the site.

resolver-bypass.meaning: DNS went to a resolver this device had not been using.
check: See the resolver address.
Check whether the device hard-codes a public resolver.
benignCauses: A device shipped with 8.8.8.8.
A guest network using a different resolver.

rogue-dhcp.meaning: A DHCP offer came from a server that is not the learned one.
check: Compare the server address with the real DHCP server.
See whether a new router was plugged in.
benignCauses: A new legitimate DHCP server during a cutover.
A phone hotspot bridging onto the LAN.

rogue-ra.meaning: A router advertisement came from a new router.
check: Compare the source with the known gateway.
See whether a new router was installed.
benignCauses: A new legitimate gateway.
A travel router plugged into the LAN.

slow-exfil.meaning: Upload volume climbed above the learned hourly pattern.
check: Compare bytes out with the same hour on earlier days.
See the destination of the upload.
benignCauses: A camera uploading more video than usual.
A backup that grew.

sni-missing.meaning: A TLS session to an unlearned address carried no server name.
check: See the destination address.
Check whether the peer is an IP-based device API.
benignCauses: A device API that uses a raw IP.
A middlebox that strips SNI.

spam-relay.meaning: Outbound mail volume exceeded the relay limit.
check: See the destination port and the recipients if present.
Check whether the device should send mail.
benignCauses: A scanner emailing documents.
A printer sending status mail.

src-spoof.meaning: The source address does not belong to the device lease.
check: Compare the source IP with the DHCP lease.
See whether the sensor is mis-attributing the device.
benignCauses: A shared NAT address.
A sensor that stamps the wrong device id.

state-cap.meaning: The engine hit a state cap and could not store more.
check: Read the cap named in the warning or anomaly.
See whether one device is creating unbounded keys.
benignCauses: A noisy device filling a destination set.
A test that exceeds a lowered cap.

stream-to-new-destination.meaning: Media-sized or streaming traffic went to a new destination.
check: See the destination and port.
Check whether a new viewer or cloud recorder was added.
benignCauses: A new phone viewing the camera.
A vendor cloud recorder.

supply-chain-suspect.meaning: An update or download matched a suspect supply-chain indicator.
check: Confirm the indicator and the file host.
See whether the download is a known firmware host.
benignCauses: A vendor host newly added to the indicator list.
A mirror of a legitimate firmware file.

check: See the peer and direction.
Check whether a boot or firmware path uses TFTP.
benignCauses: A device network-booting.
A phone loading a config by TFTP.

threat-intel-match.meaning: A name or address matched a loaded indicator.
check: Read the indicator value and source.
See whether the hit is a destination the device should avoid.
benignCauses: An indicator that is broader than the incident.
A shared CDN address also used by a listed host.

tier-silent.meaning: A detector tier this deployment asked for produced no events.
check: See which tier is named.
Check whether the sensor emits that event type.
benignCauses: A sensor that does not export TLS or DNS.
A quiet device with no traffic in that tier.

tls-on-odd-port.meaning: TLS appeared on a port this device had not used for TLS.
check: See the port.
Check whether a service moved off 443.
benignCauses: A device admin UI on 8443.
A vendor API on a high port.

tor-or-proxy.meaning: Traffic matched a Tor or proxy indicator.
check: Confirm the indicator source and value.
See whether the device should be anonymous.
benignCauses: A proxy the operator configured.
A shared address that also appears on a Tor list.

tunnel-service.meaning: A tunnel or remote-access name was new for this device.
check: See the name.
Check whether remote access was enabled.
benignCauses: A person enabling a vendor remote-support name.
A Tailscale or similar client installed on purpose.

update-from-new-source.meaning: A large download came from a source this device had not used.
check: See the source and the byte count.
Check whether it is a firmware host.
benignCauses: A firmware mirror.
A CDN fronting the vendor download.

update-over-cleartext.meaning: A large download arrived in cleartext.
check: See the port and the byte count.
Check whether the vendor offers TLS for updates.
benignCauses: A legacy firmware server on port 80.
A local cache serving images in cleartext.

upload-ratio-shift.meaning: The share of bytes sent upward shifted from the learned ratio.
check: Compare the new ratio with the learned samples.
See the destination of the upload.
benignCauses: A camera uploading a long clip.
A backup window.

upnp-port-open.meaning: A new WAN port mapping was created.
check: See the protocol and port.
Check which device requested the mapping.
benignCauses: A game or camera opening a port on purpose.
A controller refreshing an existing mapping that looked new.

vertical-scan.meaning: Many ports were touched on one host.
check: See the host and the port count.
Check whether an admin scan is running.
benignCauses: A vulnerability scan the operator started.
A controller probing one appliance.

volume-spike-hourly.meaning: Bytes in this hour exceeded the learned hourly limit.
check: Compare the hour with the same hour on earlier days.
See which destination took the bytes.
benignCauses: A camera uploading in its usual hour, but more.
A backup scheduled in that hour.

volume-spike.meaning: Bytes in the window exceeded the learned limit.
check: Compare the byte count with the limit in the explain.
See the destination.
benignCauses: A firmware download.
A camera stream.

vpn-protocol.meaning: A VPN or SSH protocol this device had not used appeared.
check: See the kind and port.
Check whether remote access was turned on.
benignCauses: An admin SSH session.
A VPN client enabled after an update.

went-silent.meaning: A device that is usually active in this hour went quiet.
check: See the gap in the anomaly.
Check power, Wi-Fi, and the sensor.
benignCauses: The device was unplugged.
The device sleeps longer than the learned gap.

wrong-time.meaning: The device was active in an hour it had not used.
check: See the hour.
Check whether a schedule or timezone changed.
benignCauses: A person using the device late.
A timezone or clock change.

zone-violation.meaning: Traffic crossed from one configured zone to another.
check: See the source and destination zones.
Check whether that path is supposed to exist.
benignCauses: A hub in one zone talking to a sensor in another.
A zone map that is coarser than the LAN.
